newsitem.title: UK: Deutsche Morgan Grenfell fighting - paper.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Morgan Grenfell fighting - paper.

text.p: Morgan Grenfell Asset Management will this week meet with key pension consultants as it fights to keep funds from leaving after the resignation of of former star manager Nicola Horlick, the Observer reported on Sunday.

It said two funds managed by MGAM, each worth more than 250 million pounds ($400 million), had indicated they would remove their money from MGAM, owned by London-based investment bank Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Horlick was suspended last Tuesday for allegedly trying to lure senior MGAM staff away with her to another bank in London.
She resigned on Thursday night and it emerged that only one week earlier she had been promoted to managing director of MGAM.
Horlick, a 35-year-old mother of five dubbed Superwoman in Britain's media, has appealed directly to Frankfurt over her suspension.
The dispute has unsettled some of MGAM's clients and the company has been reassuring customers about the future of its activities by stressing "business as usual".
Sources at the investment bank in London say the team around Horlick has remained loyal to the bank and has no intention of leaving.
